content: The document titled Tuberculosis Prevention and Care Among Refugees and Other Populations in Humanitarian Settings: An Interagency Field Guide is a comprehensive resource developed collaboratively by the World Health Organization (WHO), the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR). It provides detailed guidance on addressing tuberculosis (TB) in vulnerable populations, particularly refugees and displaced individuals in humanitarian crises. The guide is available in both electronic and print formats, with respective ISBNs 978-92-4-004208-7 and 978-92-4-004209-4. It is published under a Creative Commons license, allowing for non-commercial use, redistribution, and adaptation, provided proper citation is given. However, the use of the WHO logo is prohibited, and any adaptations must be licensed under the same or an equivalent Creative Commons license. Translations of the guide must include a disclaimer stating that the translation was not created by WHO and that the original English version remains the authoritative edition. The guide emphasizes that its content does not imply endorsement by WHO of any specific organization, product, or service. It also clarifies that the designations and material presented do not reflect any opinion on the legal status of countries, territories, or boundaries. WHO has taken all reasonable precautions to verify the information, but the responsibility for its interpretation and use lies with the reader. WHO is not liable for any damages arising from the use of the material. The guide aligns with the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, which prioritizes equality and non-discrimination, encapsulated in the principle of Leave no one behind. This principle underscores the commitment of United Nations Member States to reduce inequalities and vulnerabilities that hinder individual and collective potential. The guide acknowledges the ongoing global displacement crisis, exacerbated by conflict, poverty, and climate change, which has left millions of refugees and displaced persons at heightened risk of TB due to factors such as poverty, overcrowded living conditions, undernutrition, and limited access to healthcare. TB remains one of the leading infectious diseases globally, causing significant morbidity and mortality annually. The guide introduces innovative strategies and approaches for TB prevention and care in humanitarian settings, leveraging advancements in international research and digital technologies. It focuses on managerial and organizational aspects of TB interventions while providing links to updated clinical references. The guide aims to serve as a practical tool to alleviate the suffering and deaths caused by TB, a preventable and curable disease, particularly among refugees and displaced populations. It includes contributions from a wide range of experts and organizations, ensuring a multidisciplinary and comprehensive approach to TB care in challenging humanitarian contexts. The document also contains annexes covering various topics, such as TB drug quantification, program performance improvement, supervision checklists, communication strategies, monitoring and evaluation indicators, digital technologies in TB care, case definitions, follow-up investigations, management of treatment interruptions, community health worker tasks, specimen handling, drug resistance treatment options, people-centered care, adverse drug effects, and preventive treatment. The guide was prepared by an interagency writing group, including experts from WHO, CDC, UNHCR, and other organizations. It was informed and reviewed by independent experts and contributors from various agencies, ensuring its relevance and applicability in diverse humanitarian settings. The document also includes a glossary of terms and abbreviations to facilitate understanding of technical language and concepts related to TB prevention and care.
